run.question: We noticed our metrics dashboard shows missing data. Can you analyze the app-189-metrics-timeseries index to find any gaps in the data collection? When did data stop being collected and when did it resume? Also, what was the last request ID before the gap started?

report.summary: The app-189-metrics-timeseries index has one clear collection gap inside the authorized window (2026-11-20T05:10:17Z to 2026-11-21T05:10:17Z): documents are present at :09:00 of every hour from 2026-11-20T06:09:00Z through 2026-11-20T19:09:00Z, then none for the six hour-buckets 20:00–01:00, then present again at 2026-11-21T02:09:00Z through 2026-11-21T05:09:00Z. So the last document before the gap is at 2026-11-20T19:09:00Z and collection resumed at 2026-11-21T02:09:00Z (a ~7 hour hole, six missing hourly publications). The last request_id before the gap is REQ-37-8A4F2 on the 19:09:00Z document (whose request_id format differs from the other 17 documents); the first request_id after the gap is REQ-2037-4116. The cause of the gap is not established: no app-189 namespace, workload or configuration exists in the cluster to point at, the otel-demo pods were all created at 16:32–16:33 on 2026-11-20 (before the gap), the events returned cover only 04:23–05:08 on 2026-11-21, and the Prometheus source was unavailable during this Run. Treat the reported timestamps as the writer's @timestamp values observed in the sampled window only.

claims.text: The Elasticsearch index app-189-metrics-timeseries is green/open with 42 documents at query time and maps exactly five fields: @timestamp (date), host (keyword), metric_name (keyword), request_id (keyword) and value (float).

Inside the authorized window 2026-11-20T05:10:17Z–2026-11-21T05:10:17Z only 18 documents matched app-189-metrics-timeseries, all with metric_name=cpu_usage, spread over hosts server-1..server-5 (server-4 has 2, the others 4 each); a 1-hour date_histogram shows doc_count=1 for every hour 2026-11-20T06:00Z through 2026-11-20T19:00Z, doc_count=0 for the six buckets 2026-11-20T20:00Z, 21:00Z, 22:00Z, 23:00Z, 2026-11-21T00:00Z and 01:00Z, and doc_count=1 again for 2026-11-21T02:00Z, 03:00Z, 04:00Z and 05:00Z.

The last document before the gap is @timestamp 2026-11-20T19:09:00Z, host server-3, metric_name cpu_usage, value 56.0, request_id REQ-37-8A4F2, so the last request ID before collection stopped is REQ-37-8A4F2.

Collection resumed with a document at @timestamp 2026-11-21T02:09:00Z, host server-5, metric_name cpu_usage, value 22.0, request_id REQ-2037-4116; subsequent hourly documents follow at 2026-11-21T03:09:00Z (REQ-2116-2575), 04:09:00Z (REQ-2233-2058) and 05:09:00Z (REQ-2355-8811).

The document immediately preceding the last pre-gap document is @timestamp 2026-11-20T18:09:00Z with request_id REQ-1207-1404, i.e. the REQ-####-#### sequence ends there and the 19:09:00Z document carries the differently formatted request_id REQ-37-8A4F2.

REQ-37-8A4F2 at 2026-11-20T19:09:00Z may be an anomalous or otherwise differently produced record rather than a normal continuation of the hourly series, because its request_id does not follow the REQ-####-#### pattern used by the other 17 documents in the window; its value (56.0) and timestamp cadence (:09:00) are normal, and whether it is anomalous cannot be decided from the visible evidence.

No app-189 workload was found in the cluster state: the namespaces query returned 8 namespaces (app-102, default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly, otel-demo) with none named app-189, and none of the 26 deployments is an app-189 metrics writer/collector (app-102 holds inventory-service and loki; otel-demo holds the demo microservices plus otel-collector, prometheus, jaeger, kube-state-metrics).

All 22 otel-demo pods report status.startTime on 2026-11-20T16:32:06Z–16:33:38Z, i.e. before the 19:09–02:09 gap, so no otel-demo pod was created during the gap; two pods carry container restarts with lastState.terminated.reason=Error (kube-state-metrics-7cbf5b996-df4sz, restartCount 2; prometheus-readonly-proxy-f4866f767-62bgn, restartCount 3), but the restart counts carry no timing and cannot be tied to the gap.

A restart or rollout of the otel-demo workloads is rejected as the explanation for the 2026-11-20T19:09Z–2026-11-21T02:09Z collection gap: every otel-demo pod's startTime lies at 16:32–16:33 on 2026-11-20, about 2.6 hours before the gap began, and no pod start time falls inside the gap.

gaps: Root cause of the collection gap is unknown: no Kubernetes object in the queried cluster is shown writing, scraping or exporting to app-189-metrics-timeseries, and no evidence explains why publications at 20:09 through 01:09 on 2026-11-20/21 are absent.

The Prometheus source was unavailable during this Run: get_metric_names (twice, including the selector {__name__=~".*(189|elasticsearch|es_).*"}) and execute_prometheus_instant_query(count(up)) returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so any scraper/collector-side signal (for example scrape gaps or exporter failures) could not be checked and is unknown, not zero.

Cluster events returned by the events query cover only 2026-11-21T04:23:43Z–05:08:01Z, so there is no event coverage of the 2026-11-20T19:09Z–2026-11-21T02:09Z gap; events are not proof that nothing happened during that interval.

Only the 24-hour authorized window is visible: the index holds 42 documents total while 18 fall in the window, so whether similar gaps exist before 2026-11-20T05:10:17Z cannot be determined (the @timestamp time filter cannot be turned off).

otel-collector-789c64b9bf-tl55c log retrieval for 2026-11-20T19:00Z–2026-11-21T02:30Z hit the 4 MiB read limit and returned only the newest 100 lines (2026-11-21T02:28:58Z–02:29:59Z); its lines are self-referential gRPC 'failed to upload metrics … otel-collector:4318' warnings with no Elasticsearch sink reference, so nothing in them ties that pod to the index or to the gap, and most of the interval's logs are unread.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so no change record (deployment/config/human action) can be checked against the gap window.

Whether the writer of this index is outside the cluster entirely is unknown: the index and its document fields carry only host (server-1..server-5), metric_name, request_id and value, with no service, namespace or cluster identity.
next_steps: Identify the agent or job that writes app-189-metrics-timeseries (its scheduler/collector configuration, credentials and target endpoint) and inspect its logs for 2026-11-20T19:00Z–2026-11-21T02:30Z; that source is not present in the queried cluster state.
Confirm with the index's backing store or ILM/ingest pipeline whether the six missing hourly documents were never produced or were produced and dropped/rejected (indexing errors, backpressure).
Re-run the Prometheus checks (scrape target health for any app-189 collector, exporter error metrics) once that source is reachable, and compare the 19:09–02:09 interval against the hours before it.
Verify the odd request_id REQ-37-8A4F2 at 2026-11-20T19:09:00Z against the writer's ID-allocation scheme to decide whether it is a legitimate record or an injected/anomalous document.
